description: Rigorous CPCV+DSR+PBO validation of rebalance frequency choice for the crypto cross-sectional momentum book. Candidates: R ∈ {7, 14, 21} days (all multiples of 7 → same Thursday weekday anchor → no calendar-phase confound). Book: survivorship-debiased PT panel, identical hyperparams to validated book.
calendar_confound_note: 7/14/21 are multiples of 7; anchor is 2023-06-08 (Thursday). All three schedules rebalance ONLY on Thursdays. R=14 and R=21 land on a subset of R=7's rebal dates. This removes the weekday-phase confound from the earlier 5/10/15 sweep.

pbo_across_menu.note: N=3 configs → coarse resolution; PBO=0.981 tells how often the IS-best rebal is below-median OOS.

pbo_note: PBO=0.9807 (N=3, S=16). With only 3 highly-correlated configs (pairwise rho ~0.85), PBO mechanics are severely limited: only 3 possible lambda values (-1.099/0/+1.099), so 'passing' requires the IS-best to be UNIQUELY the best OOS config on every split. Baseline iid noise at N=3 already gives PBO ~0.88. The observed 0.98 confirms IS-winner selection is unreliable among these nearly-identical books, but is not an independent strong signal beyond what the DSR and OOS IQR already show.
verdict:
KEEP R=7 — 7/14/21 ARE STATISTICALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE.

  All three books land in the DSR WARN zone (0.90-0.92): the momentum
  edge is likely real (PSR vs 0 ~0.90) but ~3 years is insufficient
  data power to confirm it past the 0.95 bar even without multi-test
  penalty. None of the three rebal choices clears DSR > 0.95.

  OOS IQR ranges overlap broadly for all three. PBO=0.98 confirms
  IS-winner selection among these nearly-identical books is unreliable.

  Switching from R=7 to R=14 or R=21 on the basis of a higher IS
  Sharpe would be overfitting a distinction that the data cannot support.

  SECONDARY OBSERVATION (not a reason to switch): R=21 shows the
  tightest OOS IQR (0.57 to 0.93 Sharpe, 100% positive segments)
  and ~41% lower turnover vs R=7. If live costs exceed 8.5bps modeled,
  R=21 would benefit more. This is a cost argument, not a Sharpe
  argument — and it is too weak to override the indistinguishability
  finding. Retain R=7 as the incumbent non-overfit default.
  Revisit if/when the live track record provides more data.
honesty_caveats: ~3 years of data only (1102 days); low statistical power for discriminating between similar strategies.
Survivorship-debiased PT book (the honest version; includes 28 dead/delisted coins).
No real crypto bear market or liquidity crisis in the study window (2023-06 to present).
3-candidate menu gives very coarse PBO resolution (N=3 in CSCV).
The harness was validated on reference series previously; we import it unchanged.
Turnover estimates ignore intra-rebal drift (weights held fixed between rebalances, consistent with the xsec model assumption).
annualization_note: IS and OOS Sharpe/ann use sqrt(365) daily annualization (honest daily). DSR and PBO use per-period (per-day) Sharpe ratios — annualization-agnostic.
